mainTopic: The rooster-distance rule for eggs on יום טוב, the שאור/חמץ measures dispute, and covering the blood of a slaughter on יום טוב
overview: The amud opens by defining when a rooster counts as 'near' a hen: she must be able to hear him by day and be able to reach him. A river with no proper bridge blocks her, and so does a rope bridge. The גמרא then explains why רבי יוסי בן שאול's ruling about an egg found on יום טוב mentions that the nest was checked the day before, and it brings his ruling, in the name of רב, about crushed garlic left uncovered. Next it returns to the משנה's dispute about שאור and חמץ. בית שמאי learn from an extra word that the two have different measures, and בית הלל show that both words are needed. After a challenge from רבי זירא, the גמרא concludes that the dispute is only about ביעור (removal); for eating, both are a כזית. The last topic is slaughtering a חיה or עוף on יום טוב with no earth ready to cover the blood. רבה and רב יוסף explain the משנה as advice given to someone who comes to ask. They disagree about the order of digging and slaughtering in בית שמאי's advice. The amud ends with רב יהודה's condition of a shovel stuck in the ground before יום טוב, a challenge about crushing earth, and an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Nearby means the hen can hear the rooster by day
steps.stepSummary: The measure for a rooster being 'near' the hen is that she can hear his crowing in the daytime.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The rooster counts as near when the hen is close enough] that she hears his voice during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the line on the previous amud. It defines how close a rooster must be for us to assume the hen's egg came from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sound carries farther at night, so the measure uses daytime hearing, which is a shorter and stricter distance. If the hen can hear the rooster by day, we assume she mates with him. Her eggs are then fertilized eggs, which take time to form, so the egg was not newly created on יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The question it answers ('how close must the rooster be?') appears on the previous amud. It is not a new statement.

phrases.english: that she hears its voice by day.
phrases.notes: Daytime is used because sounds are harder to hear by day than at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the definition of 'a rooster nearby' begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rooster counts as near the hen if she can hear him crow during the day.

steps.title: רב מרי checks as far as sixty houses
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי acted on this rule in a real case and searched for a rooster as far as sixty houses away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי acted in a real case, checking up to sixty houses away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of a real ruling. רב מרי used the 'hearing distance' rule and went to great lengths to find a nearby rooster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One explanation, going a bit beyond what the גמרא spells out: רב מרי found an egg on יום טוב after an empty check the day before. He searched up to sixty houses away. Even though he did not find a rooster in that area, he assumed one existed farther off and permitted the egg. The story shows how widely a rooster's influence was assumed to reach.

keyTerms.meaning: acted in a real case; issued a practical ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule was applied in real practice and was not just a theory, and that the distance involved could be very large.

phrases.english: Rav Mari took action in a real case
phrases.notes: עובדא means a real-life ruling, not just a theoretical statement.

phrases.english: up to sixty houses.
phrases.notes: He checked for a rooster up to sixty houses away from the hen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'hearing distance' definition to a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, the search for a nearby rooster reached as far as sixty houses away.

steps.title: Rivers, bridges and rope bridges
steps.stepSummary: A river separates the hen from the rooster. A bridge does not. A narrow rope bridge also counts as separating them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a river, the hen does not cross it. If there is a bridge, she crosses. If there is only a rope bridge, she does not cross.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds details about what happens when the rooster is on the other side of a river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being able to hear the rooster is not enough if the hen cannot physically reach him. A river blocks her. A proper bridge lets her cross, so the rooster still counts as nearby. A thin rope bridge is treated like no bridge at all.

phrases.english: And if there is a river — she does not cross.
phrases.notes: So the rooster on the other side does not count.

phrases.english: And if there is a bridge — she crosses.
phrases.notes: So the rooster still counts as nearby.

phrases.english: And if there is a rope bridge — she does not cross.
phrases.notes: A narrow, unstable crossing is treated like a river with no bridge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a physical-access requirement on top of the hearing-distance rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A river blocks the rooster's influence unless there is a real bridge. A rope bridge does not count as a way across.

steps.title: A hen once crossed on a rope bridge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports a case where a hen actually did cross on a rope bridge.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case, and a hen crossed on a rope bridge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a report of a real event that does not fit the rule it just gave about rope bridges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that a hen can sometimes cross a rope bridge. One explanation is that this was an unusual event and one may not rely on it. So the general rule ('she does not cross a rope bridge') stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'nearby rooster' rule has two parts: the hen must be able to hear him by day, and she must be able to reach him. The rope-bridge incident was a rare exception that one may not rely on.

phrases.english: There was an incident, and she crossed on a rope bridge.
phrases.notes: This was a rare event that should not be relied on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a real case that goes against the rope-bridge rule of step 3, without cancelling that rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hen once crossed on a rope bridge, but the general rule is not changed.

steps.title: If there is no rooster, why mention checking the nest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its own explanation: if the egg was formed from the earth, it is forbidden even when the nest was never checked, so why does the ruling mention a check?
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the case? As a hen that absorbs from the earth. Then why speak specifically about someone who checked the nest? Even if he did not check, the same should apply!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוסי בן שאול's ruling and attacks the way it was explained earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of רבי יוסי בן שאול speaks about a nest that was checked on ערב יום טוב and found empty. But the גמרא explained the case as a hen without a rooster, whose egg forms quickly from the earth. Under that explanation, any egg from such a hen found on יום טוב should be suspect, whether or not anyone checked. So the detail about checking seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: how did you explain (set up) the case?
absorbs from the earth (a hen with no rooster)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about the law of eggs itself. It is asking why the wording of the ruling includes an extra detail (checking the nest) that the explanation seems to make unnecessary.

phrases.english: In what case did you establish it?
phrases.notes: Refers to the ruling of רבי יוסי בן שאול.

phrases.english: in a case where she absorbs from the earth,
phrases.notes: That is, there is no rooster nearby.

phrases.english: why specifically where he checked?
Even when he did not check, too!
phrases.notes: The ruling should apply without any check.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתָּא בִּדְסָפְנָא מֵאַרְעָא מַאי אִירְיָא בָּדַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about roosters and returns to challenge how רבי יוסי בן שאול's case was set up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי יוסי בן שאול's case is a hen without a rooster (סָפְנָא מֵאַרְעָא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason for forbidding the egg is that eggs formed from the earth develop quickly, then checking the nest the day before adds nothing. The ruling should apply even without a check, so why does it mention one?

steps.title: The check rules out an egg laid yesterday
steps.stepSummary: Without checking, we could say the egg was laid before יום טוב, so the check is needed to make the egg forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not check the nest, you could say the egg was there from yesterday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5. The check is mentioned because without it, the egg might have been laid yesterday and would be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg laid before יום טוב is fine to use on יום טוב. Only a check of the nest before יום טוב proves the egg was not there yet. So the check is what makes the egg forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: I could say / one might say

phrases.english: When he did not check,
phrases.notes: Refers to checking the nest before יום טוב.

phrases.english: say it was from yesterday.
phrases.notes: The egg may have been laid before יום טוב, so it would be permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי לָא בָּדַק, אֵימָא מֵאֶתְמוֹל הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 5 about why a check is mentioned.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that a detail in the ruling (the check) is needed to rule out another possibility.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mention of a check seemed pointless, since an egg formed from the earth is forbidden anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: The check is needed because without it the egg could have been laid yesterday and would be permitted.

steps.title: Even after a check, maybe the egg partly came out yesterday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if he checked, maybe most of the egg came out before יום טוב and went back in, which per רבי יוחנן would make it permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even when he checked, say: most of the egg came out and went back in, and follow רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 6. Even with a check, there is still a way the egg could count as laid yesterday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that if most of an egg came out of the hen before יום טוב and then slipped back in, it counts as born before יום טוב and is permitted. A check of the nest would not show this, because the egg went back inside the hen. So why should a check be enough to forbid the egg?

phrases.english: If so, when he checked as well,
phrases.notes: If we look for ways to say the egg is from yesterday.

phrases.english: say: most of it came out and it went back in,
phrases.notes: This happened before יום טוב, inside the hen, so the check would not show it.

phrases.english: and it is like רבי יוחנן's case!
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן permits such an egg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 6 by using the same kind of reasoning against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 6 that a check proves the egg was not from yesterday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we worry the egg may be from yesterday, then even after a check it might have half-emerged yesterday and returned, which רבי יוחנן permits.

steps.title: The case of רבי יוחנן is rare
steps.stepSummary: We do not worry about an egg partly coming out and going back, because that rarely happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of רבי יוחנן is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in one line. We only worry about things that happen often, and an egg coming out and going back in is rare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg simply being laid yesterday is common, so without a check we must consider it. An egg half-emerging and returning is unusual, so we ignore it. That is why the check is enough to forbid the egg.
steps.whatToRemember: A check of the nest before יום טוב is needed to forbid an egg found on יום טוב. Without a check, the egg may have been laid yesterday. We do not worry about the rare case of רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: The case of Rabbi Yochanan is not common.
phrases.notes: Rare situations are not taken into account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rarity: an uncommon case is not a reason for concern.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even after a check, the egg might count as laid yesterday under the rule of רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case of רבי יוחנן is rare, so a check is enough to forbid the egg.

steps.title: Uncovered crushed garlic is dangerous
steps.stepSummary: Another ruling from the same chain of teachers: crushed garlic that was left uncovered is dangerous to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי בן שאול said in the name of רב: crushed garlic carries the danger of being left uncovered.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just discussed a ruling of רבי יוסי בן שאול in the name of רב, it brings another one of his rulings. This one is about health, not יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushed garlic left uncovered might have been tasted by a snake, which could leave poison in it. So it falls under the danger of גילוי, uncovered food, and should not be eaten. This is a side topic, quoted only because it comes from the same speakers.

keyTerms.meaning: being left uncovered (concern that a snake drank or ate from it)

steps.confusionAlert: This ruling has nothing to do with eggs or יום טוב. It appears here only because it comes from the same teachers, רבי יוסי בן שאול in the name of רב.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said that Rav said:
phrases.notes: Same chain of teachers as the egg ruling.

phrases.english: This crushed garlic,
phrases.notes: Crushed garlic left out.

phrases.english: has the danger of being left uncovered.
phrases.notes: A snake may have left venom in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side ruling brought only because it comes from the same teachers as the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crushed garlic left uncovered is forbidden because of the danger of גילוי.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: בית שמאי on the measure for שאור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes בית שמאי: the measure for שאור is a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: שאור is a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the words of בית שמאי. This sets up the next question about their reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית שמאי, owning a כזית of שאור on פסח is forbidden, while for חמץ the measure is bigger, a כותבת (date-size). בית הלל hold that both are a כזית. The גמרא is about to explain why בית שמאי give them different measures.

keyTerms.meaning: sourdough starter, used to make other dough rise
the size of an olive (a halachic measure)

steps.confusionAlert: שאור is not regular bread. It is very strong, sour dough used to make other dough rise. חמץ is ordinary leavened bread.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: leaven is an olive-bulk.
phrases.notes: For חמץ, בית שמאי require a date-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topics and returns to the text of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, the measure for שאור is a כזית, smaller than the measure for חמץ.

steps.title: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בית שמאי give שאור and חמץ different measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source or logic behind the view of בית שמאי. This is a setup line for the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is a real request for a reason, not an attack. We want to know why שאור should have a smaller measure than חמץ.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling quoted in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason בית שמאי give שאור a smaller measure than חמץ.

steps.title: The extra word שאור teaches a different measure
steps.stepSummary: If the measures were the same, the תורה would not need to write שאור, since it could be learned by קל וחומר from חמץ. So the word שאור teaches that its measure is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the תורה should have written only חמץ and not needed שאור. I would have said: if חמץ, whose sourness is not strong, is forbidden at a כזית, then surely שאור, whose sourness is strong, is forbidden at a כזית. So why did the תורה write שאור? To tell you that the measure of one is not like the measure of the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a proof from the wording of the תורה. Because the word שאור seems extra, it must be teaching something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both measures were a כזית, the תורה could have mentioned only חמץ, and we would learn שאור through a קל וחומר: it is even stronger, so surely a כזית is forbidden. Since the תורה still wrote שאור, the word must teach that the two measures are different. בית שמאי conclude that שאור is a כזית and חמץ is larger.

keyTerms.meaning: all the more so (sign of a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי learn from the seemingly extra word שאור that שאור and חמץ have different measures: שאור is a כזית, and חמץ is larger.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic pattern in the גמרא: if something could be learned by קל וחומר but the תורה writes it anyway, the extra words must teach something new.

phrases.english: If so, let the Merciful One write leavened bread,
phrases.notes: If the measures were equal.

phrases.english: and it would not need leaven,
phrases.notes: No need to mention שאור.

phrases.english: and I would say:
phrases.notes: Introduces the קל וחומר.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה חָמֵץ שֶׁאֵין חִמּוּצוֹ קָשֶׁה — בִּכְזַיִת,
phrases.english: if leavened bread, whose leavening is not strong, is an olive-bulk,
phrases.notes: The lighter case.

phrases.aramaic: שְׂאוֹר שֶׁחִמּוּצוֹ קָשֶׁה — לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן.
phrases.english: then leaven, whose leavening is strong, all the more so.
phrases.notes: The stronger case.

phrases.english: Why do I need the leaven that the Merciful One wrote?
phrases.notes: The word seems extra.

phrases.english: To tell you:
phrases.notes: What the extra word teaches.

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיעוּרוֹ שֶׁל זֶה לֹא כְּשִׁיעוּרוֹ שֶׁל זֶה.
phrases.english: the measure of this is not like the measure of that.
phrases.notes: שאור is a כזית; חמץ is a date-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא חָמֵץ, וְלָא בָּעֵי שְׂאוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word שאור would be extra if the measures were equal, since a קל וחומר from חמץ would teach it. So it teaches that the measures are different.

steps.title: בית הלל: the word שאור alone would not teach חמץ
steps.stepSummary: For בית הלל, both words are needed. If the תורה had written only שאור, we might think a כזית applies only to it, because it is very strongly leavened. We might not apply that to ordinary חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל? They say both words are needed. If the תורה had written only שאור, I would have said its measure is a כזית because it is very strongly leavened. But חמץ, which is not as strongly leavened, I would say does not get that measure. So the תורה needed to write חמץ too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to בית הלל, who say both measures are a כזית. It explains why, in their view, the תורה still had to mention both שאור and חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, בית שמאי argued that if the measures were equal, שאור could be learned from חמץ by a קל וחומר, so writing it would be extra. בית הלל answer that neither word can be learned from the other. In this step, the special strength of שאור (its sharp leavening) means we could not learn חמץ from שאור alone.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed / it is needed (both sources are necessary)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
Its leavening is strong or intense

steps.confusionAlert: שאור is not bread. It is the very sour starter dough used to make other dough rise. That is why it is called more 'strongly leavened' than regular חמץ.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel: [both] are needed,
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: how do בית הלל explain the extra word? Their answer: both words are needed.

phrases.english: for if the Merciful One had written [only] se'or,
I would have said: [its measure is a kezayis] because its leavening is strong,
but chametz, whose leavening is not strong —
I would say not; [so] it is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית הלל's response to בית שמאי's argument about the extra word שאור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do בית הלל explain why the תורה wrote both שאור and חמץ if they have the same measure?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Neither can be learned from the other. First direction: שאור's strong leavening could make it a special case that does not teach about חמץ.

steps.title: בית הלל: the word חמץ alone would not teach שאור
steps.stepSummary: The reverse also holds. If the תורה had written only חמץ, we might think a כזית applies only to it, because it is edible. We might not apply that to שאור, which is not eaten on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only חמץ, I would have said its measure is a כזית because it is fit to eat. But שאור, which is not fit to eat, I would say does not get that measure. So the תורה needed to write both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes בית הלל's answer by showing the other direction. Writing only חמץ would not teach us about שאור either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item has its own strength. שאור is more strongly leavened, and חמץ is actually edible. Because each has a feature the other lacks, no קל וחומר works in either direction. So both words are needed even though the measure is the same. This answers בית שמאי's argument from step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: I would say not (the law would not apply)

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written [only] chametz,
[I would say a kezayis applies] because it is fit for eating.
But se'or, which is not fit for eating —
I would say not; [so] it is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided 'צריכא' argument begun in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is חמץ alone not enough?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חמץ is edible and שאור is not, so a law stated about חמץ alone might not extend to שאור.

steps.title: Challenge to בית שמאי from רבי זירא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא teaches that the verse opens with שאור and closes with חמץ to show that the two are the same. How, then, can בית שמאי give them different measures?
steps.simpleTranslation: And do בית שמאי not agree with רבי זירא? For רבי זירא said: the verse began with שאור and ended with חמץ, to tell you that שאור is the same as חמץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks בית שמאי's view using a teaching of רבי זירא. That teaching says the תורה itself treats שאור and חמץ as one and the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse (שמות יב:יט) says no שאור may be found in your houses and gives כרת for eating חמצת. Because the verse moves from one word to the other, רבי זירא learns that they are equal. If they are equal, it seems they should have the same measure, which goes against בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not hold (of a certain view)
The verse opened with... and closed with...
This is שאור, this is חמץ, meaning they are equivalent

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי לֵית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא,
phrases.english: And Beit Shammai, do they not hold of Rabbi Zeira's [teaching]?
For Rabbi Zeira said:
The verse opened with se'or and closed with chametz,
phrases.notes: שמות יב:יט: 'שאור לא ימצא בבתיכם, כי כל אוכל מחמצת...'

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר לְךָ: זֶהוּ שְׂאוֹר זֶהוּ חָמֵץ!
phrases.english: to tell you: se'or is the same as chametz!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי לֵית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining both sides, the גמרא challenges בית שמאי's different measures from a verse-based rule of equivalence.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's ruling that שאור and חמץ have different measures
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי זירא learns from the verse's structure that שאור and חמץ are identical. Identical things should share one measure.

steps.title: Everyone agrees about eating; the dispute is about removal
steps.stepSummary: For eating, all agree that the measures of שאור and חמץ are the same. The argument is only about ביעור. בית שמאי do not learn removal from eating, while בית הלל do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding eating, everyone agrees. They argue regarding removal. בית שמאי hold we do not learn the laws of removal from the laws of eating. בית הלל hold we do learn removal from eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It narrows the debate in the משנה to the measure for removing חמץ from one's house, not the measure for eating it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's rule is about eating, since the end of the verse speaks of eating חמצת. So בית שמאי accept that for eating, שאור and חמץ are the same. For removal, though, בית שמאי say the measures differ, because removal is a separate law that does not borrow from eating. בית הלל apply the eating measure to removal as well, so both are a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Removal or destruction of חמץ from one's possession
We learn or derive (one law from another)

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל in the משנה is only about removal (ביעור). For eating, all agree that שאור and חמץ share the same measure. בית שמאי do not learn removal from eating, and בית הלל do.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית שמאי reject רבי זירא. They accept his rule for eating and simply do not extend it to removal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how we read the משנה. A debate that looked like it was about eating is really about how much שאור or חמץ one must remove.

phrases.aramaic: לְעִנְיַן אֲכִילָה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְלִיגִי.
phrases.english: Regarding eating, everyone does not disagree.
When they disagree, it is regarding removal.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי: לָא יָלְפִינַן בִּיעוּר מֵאֲכִילָה,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold: we do not derive removal from eating,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי: יָלְפִינַן בִּיעוּר מֵאֲכִילָה.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel hold: we do derive removal from eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעִנְיַן אֲכִילָה כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי זירא by narrowing the scope of the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the dispute (eating versus removal)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute in the משנה is about the measure for eating, which would contradict רבי זירא.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree that the eating measures are equal. בית שמאי give different measures only for removal, because they do not learn removal from eating.

steps.title: An אמורא confirms the dispute is only about removal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא states openly that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about ביעור. For eating, everyone agrees both שאור and חמץ are a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said this way: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: The argument is about removing חמץ. But for eating, everyone agrees that both this and that are a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אמורא who said exactly what the answer in Step 16 said. This supports that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16 the גמרא answered רבי זירא's challenge by limiting the argument to ביעור. Now we see that this was not just a guess made up to escape a question. רבי יוסי בר חנינא actually taught it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated: an אמורא is quoted who said the same idea
Removing and destroying חמץ before פסח

phrases.english: It was also stated:
phrases.notes: Introduces support from an אמורא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
The dispute is regarding removal,
but regarding eating,
everyone agrees that both this and that are an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 16 with a direct statement from an אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל is only about ביעור, not eating.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A direct statement of רבי יוסי בר חנינא.

steps.title: A ברייתא also places the dispute on the verse about removal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא connects the dispute to the verse 'ולא יראה לך', which is about owning and removing חמץ. This confirms the argument is about ביעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: 'No שאור shall be seen with you, and no חמץ shall be seen with you.' This is the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל. בית שמאי say: שאור is a כזית and חמץ is a כותבת. בית הלל say: both this and that are a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second support, this time from a ברייתא. It ties the argument to the verse about not having חמץ seen in your home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'ולא יראה' is about owning חמץ, which leads to the duty of ביעור. It is not about eating. Because the ברייתא hangs the dispute on this verse, it shows the argument is about removal only.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this: support from a תנאי source
'It shall not be seen with you': the verse forbidding owning חמץ on פסח
The size of a large date, bigger than a כזית

steps.whatToRemember: All agree: for eating, both שאור and חמץ are a כזית. The argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל is only about how much requires ביעור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles רבי זירא's challenge in Step 15. The verse treats שאור and חמץ as the same for eating, and the argument lives only in the laws of removal.

phrases.english: It is also taught in a baraita this way:
"And no leaven shall be seen with you,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: and no leavened bread shall be seen with you."
This is the dispute
between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.
For Beit Shammai say:
Leaven is an olive-bulk,
and leavened bread is a large date-bulk,
and Beit Hillel say:
both this and that are an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second support, now from a ברייתא, to the same answer.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the dispute is only about ביעור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that ties the dispute to the verse ולא יראה, which is about owning and removing חמץ.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The שאור and חמץ dispute is only about ביעור. For eating, both are a כזית.

steps.title: New משנה topic: slaughtering a wild animal or bird on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, about someone who slaughters a חיה or עוף on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: One who slaughters a חיה or a bird on יום טוב, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה. It is setting up a close look at the משנה's exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After slaughtering a חיה or עוף, one must cover the blood (כיסוי הדם). The משנה is about a case where no earth was prepared before יום טוב. בית שמאי say he may dig with a tool and cover the blood. בית הלל say he should not slaughter unless he prepared earth beforehand.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild animal, such as a deer
The מצוה to cover the blood of a slaughtered חיה or עוף

phrases.english: One who slaughters an undomesticated animal or a bird
on a Festival, etc.
phrases.notes: A shortened quote from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שאור and חמץ topic and opens the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's case: slaughtering a חיה or עוף on יום טוב without prepared earth for covering the blood.

steps.title: Does 'one who slaughters' mean only after the fact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the word השוחט ('one who slaughtered') to mean that digging is allowed only after the fact. It would not be allowed from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who slaughters.' Does this mean only after the fact, yes, but from the start, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at how the משנה is worded. It suggests that the word השוחט describes something already done. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה had meant it was fully allowed, it could have said 'one may slaughter.' Saying 'one who slaughtered' sounds like a case after the fact. That would mean even בית שמאי do not allow slaughtering from the start without earth ready.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact, once it was already done
From the start, as a planned action

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a final ruling. The גמרא is only testing a possible reading of the משנה's wording, and the next step attacks it.

phrases.english: "One who slaughters":
after the fact, yes, but ab initio, no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the wording השוחט mean the משנה is only about an after-the-fact case?

steps.title: The end of the משנה implies slaughtering is allowed from the start
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says בית הלל rule 'he may not slaughter.' This implies the first opinion, בית שמאי, says he may slaughter even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: 'And בית הלל say: he may not slaughter.' This implies that the first תנא holds that he may slaughter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from Step 20. It uses the end of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל argue about whether one may slaughter from the start. So the first opinion, בית שמאי, must be allowing exactly that. This goes against the idea that השוחט means only after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at the end of the משנה
The first opinion stated in the משנה, here בית שמאי

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
"And Beit Hillel say: He may not slaughter."
By inference, the first tanna
holds he may slaughter!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: לֹא יִשְׁחוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the after-the-fact reading in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that השוחט means digging is allowed only after the fact.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית הלל say 'he may not slaughter,' so they must be arguing about slaughtering from the start. That means בית שמאי allow slaughtering from the start, which contradicts the after-the-fact reading.

steps.title: בית הלל really mean 'do not slaughter and then cover'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בית הלל's phrase 'he may not slaughter' is really about the covering: one may not slaughter and then cover. So the משנה can still be about a case after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. When בית הלל say 'he may not slaughter,' they mean 'he may not slaughter and cover.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the problem from the last step. It says that the main point of בית הלל's words is the covering, not the slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the whole משנה stays 'after the fact.' The person already slaughtered, and the argument is only whether he may now dig and cover. בית שמאי say he may cover, while בית הלל say he may not. Because of this, there is no hint that בית שמאי allow slaughtering from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult (an opening phrase for an answer)
he is saying / this is what he means

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
He (בית הלל) is saying: one may not slaughter and cover.
phrases.notes: The stress falls on the covering, which comes after the slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21 by rereading בית הלל's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He may not slaughter' implies that בית שמאי allow slaughtering from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'He may not slaughter' means 'may not slaughter and cover.' The whole argument is about covering after the fact.

steps.title: The end of the משנה shows בית הלל allow covering after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says בית הלל agree that if he already slaughtered, he digs and covers. So the first part of the משנה cannot be about after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: 'And they agree that if he slaughtered, he digs with a shovel and covers.' This proves that the first part of the משנה is not about after the fact!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 22 by pointing to the last line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said that בית הלל forbid covering even after the fact. But the סיפא says that בית הלל agree he may cover once he has slaughtered. So the argument in the רישא must be about what to do from the start, and that brings back the problem with the word השוחט.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at / say the end of the משנה
after the fact (once it was already done)

phrases.english: Say the end of the משנה:
And they agree that if he slaughtered,
he may dig with a shovel and cover.
This proves that the first part
is not about after the fact!

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית הלל changed their mind in the סיפא. The סיפא only shows that the רישא was never about after the fact. It was about what to do from the start.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 22 using the end of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 22 that בית הלל forbid covering even after slaughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא says בית הלל allow covering after slaughter. So the רישא must be about the start, and השוחט is a problem again.

steps.title: רבה: השוחט means someone who comes to ask
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that השוחט refers to a person who comes to ask a רב what to do. בית שמאי tell him to slaughter, dig, and cover. בית הלל say he may slaughter only if he prepared earth before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This is what the משנה means. A slaughterer comes to ask. What should the רב tell him? בית שמאי say he tells him: 'Slaughter, dig, and cover.' בית הלל say: He may not slaughter unless he had earth ready from before יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new answer for the word השוחט. It describes a person asking before he acts, so the משנה is about what to do from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: השוחט does not mean 'one who already slaughtered.' It names the person who wants to slaughter and asks for guidance. Now the רישא is clearly about the start, which fits the סיפא. In רבה's version, בית שמאי say the order is: slaughter first, then dig.

keyTerms.meaning: to ask advice / consult a רב
while it was still day (before יום טוב began)

phrases.english: רבה said: this is what it means:
A slaughterer who comes to consult —
what does one tell him?
בית שמאי say: he tells him:
Slaughter, dig, and cover.
phrases.notes: In this order, slaughtering comes before digging.

phrases.english: And בית הלל say: he may not slaughter
unless he had
earth prepared from while it was still day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after step 22 was rejected in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (השוחט means a person coming to ask)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: השוחט means someone who already slaughtered, so the case is after the fact.
steps.terutzMaskana: השוחט means someone asking before acting. The argument is about the start. בית שמאי say: slaughter, dig, cover.

steps.title: רב יוסף: same reading, but dig before slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף agrees that השוחט means someone who comes to ask. But in his version, בית שמאי tell him: 'Go dig, slaughter, and cover.' The digging comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is what the משנה means. A slaughterer comes to ask. What should the רב tell him? בית שמאי say he tells him: 'Go dig, slaughter, and cover.' בית הלל say: He may not slaughter unless he had earth ready from before יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second version of the same answer. The only change is the order of the steps in בית שמאי's advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree that the משנה is about a person asking before he acts, and that בית הלל require earth prepared before יום טוב. They differ only on בית שמאי. רבה says slaughter first and then dig, while רב יוסף says dig first and then slaughter. This step only gives the two versions. It does not yet explain why each one chose his order.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read השוחט. Both say it is a person who comes to ask, so the משנה is about what to do from the start. For בית שמאי, רבה says: slaughter, dig, cover. רב יוסף says: dig, slaughter, cover. For בית הלל, both say he needs earth prepared before יום טוב.

phrases.english: רב יוסף said: this is what it means:
A slaughterer who comes to consult,
what does one tell him?
בית שמאי say: he tells him:
Go dig, slaughter, and cover,
phrases.notes: Here digging comes before slaughtering. This is the difference from רבה.

phrases.english: And בית הלל say: he may not slaughter
unless he had
earth prepared from while it was still day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel version of רבה's answer that changes only the order of steps for בית שמאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (same as רבה), with a different order of actions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבה, בית שמאי would say slaughter first and then dig.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי say dig first, then slaughter and cover. בית הלל still require earth prepared before יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי asks if the dispute depends on רבי זירא's rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests that רבה and רב יוסף disagree over רבי זירא's teaching in the name of רב. That teaching says the blood needs earth below it and earth above it, learned from the word בעפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Shall we say that you and רבה disagree about רבי זירא's teaching in the name of רב? רבי זירא said in the name of רב: A person who slaughters must put earth below and earth above. The verse says, 'He shall pour out its blood and cover it in earth.' It does not say 'earth,' but 'in earth.' This teaches that the slaughterer must put earth below and earth above.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a possible reason why רבה and רב יוסף gave different instructions to the person asking. He quotes רבי זירא's rule as the possible source of their disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יוסף's version, the person digs first so that earth is already under the blood. אביי wonders if this is because רב יוסף holds you need earth below, as רבי זירא taught. The proof comes from the extra letter ב in בעפר, which means 'inside earth,' with earth surrounding the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (introduces a suggested explanation)
In earth (the extra ב teaches earth on both sides)
The מצוה of covering the blood

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי זירא's rule explains why anyone would dig before slaughtering. You need earth ready under the blood, not only on top of it.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Shall we say that the Master and Rabba

phrases.aramaic: בִּדְרַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב קָא מִפַּלְגִיתוּ,
phrases.english: disagree about the teaching of Rabbi Zeira in the name of Rav?
For Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav:
One who slaughters must put earth below
phrases.notes: Below the blood

phrases.english: and earth above,
as it says: 'He shall pour out its blood and cover it in earth.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא יז:יג

phrases.english: It does not say 'earth,' but 'in earth.'
This teaches that the slaughterer must
put earth below and earth above.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מָר וְרַבָּה בִּדְרַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב קָא מִפַּלְגִיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the underlying reason for the two versions in Steps 24 and 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the רבה and רב יוסף dispute come from whether one accepts רבי זירא's rule of earth below and above?

steps.title: אביי spells out the suggested split
steps.stepSummary: אביי spells out his suggestion: רב יוסף holds like רבי זירא, and רבה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is, the Master holds like רבי זירא, and רבה does not hold like רבי זירא?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his question by stating plainly who would hold what. This sets up רב יוסף's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you need earth below, you must dig first, which is רב יוסף's order. If you only need earth above, you could slaughter first and dig later. אביי thinks רבה's version fits that second approach.

phrases.english: that the Master holds like Rabbi Zeira,
and Rabba does not hold like Rabbi Zeira?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's question from Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Confirmation that the dispute is whether one accepts רבי זירא's rule.

steps.title: Both accept רבי זירא; רבה worries about wasted digging
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that he and רבה both accept רבי זירא. Their disagreement is about how בית שמאי advise the person asking. For רבה, בית שמאי let him slaughter first only if loose earth is already lying beneath. If there is none, they do not let him dig first, because he might change his mind and not slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Both I and רבה hold like רבי זירא. Here is what we disagree about. רבה holds: if there is earth below already, yes, he may slaughter. If not, no. We worry that perhaps he will change his mind and not slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rejects אביי's suggestion. He says the disagreement is not about רבי זירא's rule, and he explains רבה's real reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions explain בית שמאי's advice, and both agree that earth must be below the blood. רבה says בית שמאי would not tell him to dig first, because he might dig and then decide not to slaughter, and then he would have dug on יום טוב for nothing. That is why רבה's order is 'slaughter, dig, cover'. It works only where earth is already lying below; if there is none, he may not slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: Both according to me and according to רבה
Perhaps he will change his mind

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֵּין לְדִידִי בֵּין לְרַבָּה
phrases.english: He said to him: Both according to me and according to Rabba
we hold like Rabbi Zeira.
And here is what we disagree about:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה סָבַר: אִי אִיכָּא עָפָר לְמַטָּה — אִין,
phrases.english: Rabba holds: if there is earth below already, yes (he may slaughter);
if not, no.
We worry that perhaps he will change his mind and not slaughter.
phrases.notes: Then the digging would have been for nothing on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לְדִידִי בֵּין לְרַבָּה אִית לַן דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proposed basis and gives the real one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both accept רבי זירא. The dispute is about a practical worry. רבה fears pointless digging if the person changes his mind.

steps.title: רב יוסף: allowing the digging protects שמחת יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that his own approach is better. If we do not allow digging, people will avoid slaughtering and miss out on שמחת יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to me, on the contrary, this is better: if you do not permit him, he will come to hold back from שמחת יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the reason for his own version, where the person digs first and then slaughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף turns the concern around. The bigger danger is not wasted digging. The bigger danger is that a person without prepared earth will skip having meat on יום טוב. Allowing him to dig keeps the יום טוב joyful.

keyTerms.meaning: The joy of יום טוב (including eating meat)

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבה and רב יוסף accept that blood needs earth below and above. They differ only in explaining בית שמאי. רבה worries the person may dig for nothing, so in his reading בית שמאי allow slaughter only where earth already lies below. רב יוסף worries the person will lose שמחת יום טוב, so in his reading בית שמאי allow digging first. בית הלל, in both versions, require earth prepared before יום טוב.

phrases.english: And according to me, on the contrary, this is preferable,
since if you do not permit him,
he will come to hold back from the joy of Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's answer by giving his side of the reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף permits digging first, to protect שמחת יום טוב.

steps.title: רב יהודה limits the case to a shovel stuck in the ground before Yom Tov
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the סיפא of the משנה: if he already slaughtered, he digs with a דקר and covers. רב יהודה limits this to a case where the shovel was stuck in the ground from before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that if he slaughtered, he digs with a shovel and covers. רבי זריקא said in the name of רב יהודה: This is only when he has a shovel stuck in the ground from while it was still day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: the last part of the משנה, about the case after the fact. רב יהודה adds a condition to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the shovel was already stuck in the ground before יום טוב, the earth around it was presumably already loosened (the text does not spell out the reason). So pulling it out to get earth involves less new work on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A digging tool, shovel or pick
While it was still day (before יום טוב began)

phrases.english: And they agree that if he slaughtered,
he digs with a shovel and covers.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika said in the name of Rav Yehuda:
This is only when he has a shovel stuck in the ground
from while it was still day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדִים שֶׁאִם שָׁחַט שֶׁיַּחְפּוֹר בַּדָּקָר וִיכַסֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the סיפא of the משנה, which was cited in Step 23, and adds a limiting condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Digging to cover after the fact is allowed only if a דקר was stuck in the ground before יום טוב.

steps.title: But digging still crushes earth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's condition. Even with a shovel already stuck in the ground, he still crushes clumps of earth (כתישה) when he digs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is still doing crushing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's condition from Step 30.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shovel that was already in place solves some problems. But digging up earth still breaks clumps, which is a forbidden kind of work called כתישה. So how does the stuck shovel make digging allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: Crushing or breaking up clumps (a forbidden kind of work)

phrases.english: But he is still doing crushing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's condition.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's rule that a shovel stuck in the ground before יום טוב makes digging allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Digging still breaks clumps of earth, which is forbidden כתישה, so the stuck shovel does not solve the problem.

steps.title: The answer in the name of רב begins
steps.stepSummary: The answer to the כתישה challenge begins. רב חייא בר אשי quotes רב. The content of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer to the כתישה problem. Only the name of the speaker appears here, and the actual answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line opens the reply to Step 31. The next amud shows how רב explains why the digging is still allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav:
phrases.notes: The answer itself continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the כתישה challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Answer continues on the next amud
